objective: Keep advancing the Maples animation/VFX changes from first principles. Treat the previous rescue pass as only an intermediate draft, not a destination. Re-inspect the current presentation and push the player-facing result materially further. Start from silhouette, weight, timing, trajectory, contact, and aftermath, and ask what would make movement, melee, dodge, hurt reaction, casting, projectile travel/impact, and recovery read as a cohesive commercial-indie action-RPG instead of incremental polish. Preserve what is genuinely working, but do not protect prior implementation choices merely because they exist. Make the next delta unmistakable at normal gameplay camera distance. Prioritize stronger motion composition, body commitment, readable attack arcs, directional contact, authored recovery, distinct spell grammars, and secondary motion that starts and stops with intent. Avoid particle spam, generic glow, and tiny offsets. Before returning the patch, compare the proposed result against the current one from a skeptical player's perspective and keep iterating until the improvement should be obvious without explanation.
role: principal gameplay animation director and real-time VFX lead continuing a first-principles commercial-quality pass; expert in motion design, combat feel, Three.js procedural animation, authored impact language, particles, trails, and performance-conscious browser rendering
relevant_context: Maples is an original Three.js browser action-RPG targeting commercial-indie showcase quality. The owner previously rejected a pass because the visual delta was not obvious enough. A stronger first-principles rescue pass followed, and this job must continue advancing that direction rather than merely restating it. Gameplay authority remains sacred: do not alter damage, hit windows, cooldowns, movement authority, enemy AI, camera, input, UI contracts, or asset licensing. Animation/VFX consume authoritative state/events. You may substantially rethink presentation architecture within the allowlist. Mobile/low quality must retain the same design language at reduced cost. Fewer better effects are preferred to particle spam. Make changes perceptible at normal gameplay camera distance.
acceptance_criteria: Use silhouette, weight, timing, trajectory, contact, and aftermath as the decision framework for every major change.

Advance ordinary locomotion beyond the prior pass: acceleration, braking, turning, idle settle, upper/lower body counter-motion, and secondary follow-through should communicate mass and intent immediately.
Advance melee attacks as complete motion phrases with stronger anticipation, body commitment, acceleration, contact, recoil/follow-through, and recovery while preserving authoritative timing.
Make the three-hit chain visibly distinct at normal camera distance, with the third hit clearly heavier in silhouette, arc, and aftermath without changing balance.
Real hits and misses must diverge visually through target-relative directional contact, recoil/follow-through, debris/dust/shock grammar, and aftermath rather than only intensity or color.
Weapon trails must describe actual path and speed with authored width, taper, breakup, and persistence that improves readability rather than obscures it.
Dodge should read as compression -> explosive displacement -> settle; hurt reactions should interrupt posture and recover weight clearly without creating a competing state machine.
Spell, projectile, healing, and level-up effects should each have distinct shape, motion, timing, and dissipation grammar rather than palette swaps.
Secondary cape/hair/torso motion must reinforce starts, stops, turns, attacks, and landings, then visibly settle instead of becoming ambient wobble.
Prefer fewer, better directional particles and temporal layers over primitive spam, bloom, or brightness as the main spectacle source.
Keep shared resources, bounded pools, reusable buffers, and coherent mobile/low-quality budgets; avoid obvious hot-loop allocation regressions.
Do not stop when tests pass. Perform a skeptical player-perspective visual self-review, identify the three weakest remaining moments, improve them, and only then return the patch.
Return only an allowlisted apply-clean unified diff and behavior-focused tests where appropriate. No unrelated refactors.
